dialogue:
[doctor] good morning ! i'm doctor hill . you must be teddy , and this is mom ?
[parent] yes , i'm april , her mom . her dad kenji is parking the car .
[doctor] no rush . so teddy is here for her four-year well visit . just to confirm , full name theodora vance-nakamura , date of birth march 9th , 2022 ?
[parent] that's right . and my cell is still 614-555-0187 .
[doctor] perfect . how has she been doing ?
[parent] really well . she started at little acorns montessori in the fall , three mornings a week . her teacher , miss priya , says she's the chattiest kid in the room .
[doctor] any concerns about speech or hearing ?
[parent] none . she bosses her brother bodhi around all day . he's seven , second grade at indian run elementary .
[doctor] and how is she eating ?
[parent] she's a grazer . goldfish crackers , juice boxes at daycare , and her grandma , mrs . nakamura , spoils her with sweets every sunday .
[doctor] is she active ?
[parent] very . we walk up the hill to the park behind our house most evenings .
[doctor] love that . so , her growth chart . she's 18.6 kilos , about the 89th percentile , and 103 centimeters , around the 52nd . that puts her bmi at the 92nd percentile , which is the overweight range for her age . no diet , but we'll use the 5-2-1-0 plan : five fruits and veggies , two hours or less of screens , one hour of play , zero sugary drinks . swap the juice for water or milk .
[parent] okay . i'll talk to grandma .
[doctor] blood pressure is 98 over 58 , normal . vision was 20/40 in both eyes , a pass at her age . i hear a soft musical murmur , grade 2/6 . it sounds like a still's murmur , an innocent flow sound , nothing to worry about .
[doctor] she's due for dtap , polio , mmr and chickenpox today . has she seen a dentist ?
[parent] not yet .
[doctor] i'd like her to see dr . o'callaghan at smile sprouts . and i'll see her back in six months to recheck her weight .
[parent] thanks , dr . hill . can you sign the daycare health form for little acorns ?
[doctor] absolutely .

ROBINA COAST HOSPITAL - CHILDREN'S EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
ED Discharge Summary and Letter to GP

NGATA, Kahu Rawiri    UR: 7714302    DOB: 02-Feb-2018 (8y 7m)    Sex: M
Medicare: 2953 61847 2 / 3    IHI: 8003 6081 7742 0195
Address: 17 Banksia Cres, Burleigh Heads QLD 4220
NOK: Mere NGATA (mother), mob 0491 570 156
Arrival: 13/09/2026 18:05    Discharge: 13/09/2026 22:40
Treating clinician: Dr Tomás Ferreira-Lynch, Paediatric Emergency Registrar
GP: Dr Leonie Strong, Palm Beach Family Medical, fax (07) 5550 4417

Dear Dr Strong,

Thank you for seeing Kahu, an 8 year old right-handed boy who presented on Sunday 13 September 2026 after a fall while trampolining. At about 5 pm he was on the family trampoline in the backyard with his older sister Matariki (aged 11) when he bounced off the edge and landed on his outstretched right hand on the grass. Immediate pain and swelling of the distal forearm. No head strike, no LOC, no other injuries. Mum (Mere) brought him in by car.

On arrival pain 6/10, settling to 2/10 after oral paracetamol 360 mg and ibuprofen 240 mg (weight 24 kg, 50th centile).

Examination: alert, GCS 15/15, afebrile. Right wrist: dorsal swelling and point tenderness over the distal radius about 3 cm proximal to the wrist crease; no deformity; skin intact. Radial pulse strong, cap refill < 2 s. Median, ulnar and radial nerve motor and sensory function intact (OK sign, thumbs up, crossed fingers). Elbow, clavicle and scaphoid non-tender.

Imaging: XR right wrist and forearm (Acc# RCH-XR-26-0918834) - torus (buckle) fracture of the distal right radial metaphysis, dorsal cortex, no displacement or angulation. Physis normal, no Salter-Harris injury. Ulna intact. Reported by Dr Anh Nguyen, radiologist.

Diagnosis: Closed torus fracture, distal right radius.

Management and advice:
- Removable wrist splint fitted; wear for 3 weeks, may remove for bathing. Sling for comfort for 48 hours.
- No trampoline, monkey bars or contact sport for 4 weeks.
- Regular paracetamol and ibuprofen for 2-3 days, then as needed.
- School note provided for Burleigh Ridge State School (class teacher Mr Hamish Grey).
- Family given the buckle fracture fact sheet: https://kids.robinacoast.example.org.au/factsheets/wrist-buckle

Follow-up: no fracture clinic required. Please review in 3 weeks (around 04/10/2026) to remove the splint. Return to ED if pain is increasing, fingers become numb, pale or blue, or the splint becomes tight.

Safeguarding: history consistent with the injury and developmental stage; no concerns identified.

Kind regards,

Dr Tomás Ferreira-Lynch
Paediatric Emergency Registrar, Provider No. 4471829T
Robina Coast Hospital, ph (07) 5550 1234
Dictated 13.09.26 / typed 14.09.26 /KJ

dialogue:
[doctor] Hi, I'm Dr. Ortiz-Bermúdez. You must be Mom, and this little guy is Rowan?
[parent] Yes, I'm Kayla. He's seven months old and he's been so congested since Tuesday.
[doctor] Just to confirm, that's Rowan Elias Young, born March 2nd, 2026?
[parent] Yep.
[doctor] Tell me what's been going on.
[parent] It started as a runny nose, then the cough got worse. Last night he was breathing really fast and he's only taking half his bottles. His sister Nevaeh had the same cold last week, she picks everything up at Sunny Patch.
[doctor] Any fever? Wet diapers?
[parent] 100.8 yesterday, I gave him Tylenol, 2.5 mL. Maybe four wet diapers today, usually it's like eight.
[doctor] Who else lives at home?
[parent] Me, the two kids, and my grandpa, Walt Parkinson. He's 91 and he has Parkinson's, so I help take care of him too.
[doctor] That's a lot on your plate. Does anyone smoke in the house?
[parent] Grandpa smokes his pipe in the living room. I keep asking him to go out on the porch but Mr. Parkinson does what Mr. Parkinson wants.
[doctor] Smoke exposure really does make these infections worse in babies, so let's keep working on that. Let me listen to him.
[doctor] His oxygen is 93% on room air and he's breathing about 56 times a minute. I hear crackles and some wheezing on both sides, and he's pulling in a little between the ribs. The RSV swab came back positive.
[parent] So it's RSV. Does he need to stay in the hospital?
[doctor] Not right now. Young babies with RSV usually peak around day three to five. His oxygen is above 92% and he's drinking enough if we keep it up. Nasal saline and suction before every feed, smaller feeds more often, and no pipe smoke indoors.
[parent] Okay.
[doctor] If he's breathing faster than 60, sucking in at the neck, has blue lips, or fewer than three wet diapers in a day, go straight to the ER at Mesa Vista Children's. Otherwise I'll see him back Monday, October 12th. The nurse line is 915-555-0119.
[parent] Thank you, Dr. Ortiz.

O: T 100.2 F, HR 152, RR 56, SpO2 93% RA, Wt 7.9 kg (40th %ile; 45th %ile at WCC on 09/04/2026). Mild nasal flaring, subcostal and intercostal retractions; diffuse fine crackles and expiratory wheeze bilaterally; cap refill < 2 s; MMM, AFOF. Rapid RSV Ag (Acc# 26-RSV-04417) POSITIVE.

A:
1. Acute bronchiolitis due to RSV, mild-moderate; SpO2 >= 92%, hydration adequate for outpatient care.

P: Supportive care - nasal saline and bulb suction before feeds, small frequent feeds. No albuterol or steroids. Natural course in young infants reviewed (peak day 3-5).
